fr.recommendations:
• Install a clearly visible address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Install reflective markers along both sides of the driveway so responders can navigate it quickly at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Post the property address at the point where the driveway meets the road, not only at the residence, due to the length of the driveway.
• Keep the full width of the driveway clear of encroaching vegetation so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Trim vegetation along the driveway edges to maintain a clear overhead and side clearance for larger emergency vehicles.
• Identify and mark a turnaround area near the residence so apparatus can reverse direction without becoming blocked at a dead end.
• Mark or communicate to responders the location of both detached structures, as secondary structures may not be immediately visible from the driveway.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and each detached structure so responders can move between buildings on foot without obstruction.
• Cut back dense vegetation growing close to any structure to give responders room to work around the building perimeter.
• Identify the water feature location and mark any unmarked edges or drop-offs near access paths so responders moving in low light do not encounter them unexpectedly.
• Establish and communicate an alternate foot-access route to the rear

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or touch any structure in the cluster.
• Thin scattered trees closest to the structures to create open gaps between the tree canopy and the buildings.
• Cut back brush growing near the outside walls of any structure in the cluster.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or within a few feet of any structure.
• Thin shrubs scattered across the property where they grow close together and connect to areas near the structures.
• Cut grass around the structures short and keep it mowed regularly.
• Clear branches and shrubs along the driveway so a fire truck can pass through without vegetation touching the vehicle.
• Trim overhanging branches along the full length of the driveway so they do not block vertical clearance.
• Remove brush and shrubs growing along the driveway edges that could carry fire toward the structures.
• Separate vegetation growing between the structures in the cluster so open ground exists between each building.
• Cut back mixed vegetation where it grows up against or crowds any structure in the cluster.
• Maintain mowed or cleared grass between structures so fire cannot travel along the ground from one building to another.
